steps.say: The Sun is a star. The Earth is a planet that orbits the Sun once a year.

figure.alt: The Sun, the Earth and the Moon.

steps.say: The Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours.
The side facing the Sun has day. The side facing away has night.
As the Earth spins, the Sun seems to rise in the east. Later it seems to set in the west.
The Moon orbits the Earth about once every 4 weeks. It reflects light from the Sun.

options.text: The Sun goes out at night.
options.why: The Sun shines all the time.

options.text: Our side of the Earth faces away from the Sun.

options.why: The Moon does not cause night.

hints: The Earth spins all the time.
Only half of the Earth faces the Sun.
Where is your side facing at night?
check.explanation: At night, our side of the Earth has turned to face away from the Sun.

check.prompt: The Earth takes about 365 days to ___ the Sun once.
hints: The Earth travels in a big loop.
The loop goes all the way past the Sun and back.
The science word starts with o.
check.explanation: The Earth orbits the Sun once every year, which is about 365 days.
